mcp__Notion__notion_update_view
tools.description:
Update a view's name, filters, sorts, or display configuration.

Use "fetch" to get view IDs from database responses. Only include fields
you want to change. The "configure" param uses the same DSL as create_view.
Use CLEAR to remove settings:
- CLEAR FILTER — remove all filters
- CLEAR QUICK FILTER — remove all quick filters, or name properties to remove only theirs (CLEAR QUICK FILTER "Status")
- CLEAR SORT — remove all sorts
- CLEAR GROUP BY — remove grouping. Boards reject it; use GROUP BY with another property instead (CLEAR SUB GROUP BY still works).
- CLEAR SUB GROUP BY — remove board sub-grouping
- CLEAR ICON — remove the view's tab icon
- CLEAR SUBSET FILTER — remove an XL view's subset filter


Set board or gallery card layout with CARD LAYOUT default or CARD LAYOUT compact. Set gallery card size without a cover property with CARD SIZE small, medium, or large. BY OPTION and BY GROUP apply only to status properties and rollups that return status values (Show original or Show unique). For select and multi_select properties, omit both modifiers, even if the property is named "Status" (for example, GROUP BY "Status").

See notion://docs/view-dsl-spec resource for full syntax (readable via your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or by passing the URI to the Notion "fetch" tool).

<example description="Rename">{"view_id": "abc123", "name": "Sprint Board"}</example>
<example description="Update filter">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "FILTER "Status" = "Done""}</example>
<example description="Add quick filters without criteria">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "QUICK FILTER "Status", "Assignee""}</example>
<example description="Clear filter, add sort">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "CLEAR FILTER; SORT BY "Created" DESC"}</example>
<example description="Update grouping">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "GROUP BY "Status" BY GROUP SHOW EMPTY; SUB GROUP BY "Priority"; CARD LAYOUT compact"}</example>

```ts
mcp__Notion__notion_update_view(args: {
// View configuration DSL string. Supports FILTER, QUICK FILTER, SORT BY, GROUP BY, SUB GROUP BY, CARD LAYOUT, CARD SIZE, CALENDAR BY, TIMELINE BY, MAP BY, CHART, FORM, SHOW, HIDE, COVER, WRAP CELLS, WRAP PROPERTIES, FREEZE COLUMNS, ICON, WIDTH, SUBSET, and CLEAR directives. BY OPTION and BY GROUP apply only to status properties and rollups that return status values (Show original or Show unique). For select and multi_select properties, omit both modifiers, even if the property is named "Status" (for example, GROUP BY "Status").
configure?: string,
// Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.
instructions_version?: string,
// New name for the view.
name?: string,
// For tracking only: the name of the agent skill you are following for this task, such as notion-meeting-prep. Omit if you are not following a skill.
skill?: string,
// The view to update. Accepts a view:// URI, a Notion URL with ?v= parameter, or a bare UUID.
view_id: string,
[key: string]: any,
}): Promise<unknown>;
```

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_backtest
tools.description:
Run a backtest of an indicator rule on one stock or ETF, on daily bars.

        A rule the lab's cards hold runs as a circuit of them on the lab's engine, as the lab's assistant builds it
        for the same words, over the span asked: the optimizer tries the settings around the rule on the two years
        before and picks the best, the forward test runs that pick against simply holding, and the autopsy deals the
        test's days again in new orders. It holds the entry's conditions (all must hold to buy), one exit condition, a
        confirming filter, a target and a holding limit (an indicator, or one of its lines, against a level, another
        of its lines or the price; two moving averages crossing); a short side runs long, a share of the account as
        the whole account, a commission as the lab's costs and a stop as the lab's Stop Loss card, each said in one
        line. Its card draws the circuit, lights each card as the run reaches it, shows the result under it, the
        surface of the settings the optimizer tried with its pick, and the fan of the dealt days; a change to a card's
        settings on the card runs it again. Its answer's kind is primitives_run, and get_primitives_run_progress
        follows it. Tuning window by window on past years is start_walkforward. Two exit conditions in one list run on
        the backtester, as before.

        No setting has to be settled before it runs: what the request leaves open (the stock or fund, the
        history, the entry and exit levels, the costs) runs with sensible defaults, which the result names in
        one short line; a change is a new run. `question` titles its report. The call waits for the run while it
        is likely to finish inside it, then answers with the result; the run's card in the chat shows the result
        or, for a longer run, how far it is, and fills in by itself, with the next steps as choices. A run
        started here needs no `show_report_card`.

        Every account runs it within a daily allowance; a refused call does not count, and get_started and
        every run's answer give today's count.

        A run takes about 30 seconds to 3 minutes. The call returns
        `{task_id, status, kind, dashboard_url}` at once.
        `get_backtest_progress(task_id)` reports progress; when the run has
        finished, its answer carries `result`: the summary in words and, for
        a run of a year or longer, a few rounded figures (the run's return
        next to simply holding the same stock over the same dates, Sharpe,
        worst drop, trades), and `report_url`, the full report.

        `list_indicators()` lists the indicators, their settings and the
        columns each one computes. An indicator is written
        `{"id": "rsi", "params": {"length": 14}}`.

        Args:
            ticker: Stock or ETF symbol (uppercase).
            entry_indicator / entry_conditions: The entry signal (required).
            exit_indicator / exit_conditions: Optional.
            confirmation_indicator / confirmation_conditions: Optional, a filter that
                must also hold on the day the entry fires. The common use is a trend
                filter: a two-day RSI pullback that buys only while the close is above
                its 100-day average is written as confirmation_indicator
                {"id": "sma", "params": {"length": 100}} and confirmation_conditions
                [{"column": "close", "operator": ">", "value": "SMA_100"}].
            timeframe: '1d' (daily bars, the only timeframe this connector runs).
            duration: The history tested, a span back from today: '60d', '6m',
                '1y', '2y', '3y', '5y', '10y' or 'max'; left out, or as given when the person named no span, the last year, said once with the longer run as the next step
                (on the lab's cards the last three years, said in one line; on the
                backtester the whole history held, up to 30 years).
                There is no start date: 'since 2010' is '10y' or 'max', and the
                figures carry the years the run covered.
            direction: 'long' | 'short' | 'both'.
            position_sizing: 'fixed' | 'percent_equity' (the default, as in
                the QuanterLab UI).
            risk_per_trade: Share of the account each trade uses. 1.0, the
                default, is the whole account, as in the QuanterLab UI; a
                smaller share leaves the rest in cash and scales the result
                down with it. Sizing across several positions (Kelly, GARCH,
                fixed) is handled in QuanterLab's portfolio and paper-trading
                tools.
            stop_loss_pct / take_profit_pct / max_holding_days: Optional exits.
            spread_bps / commission_per_trade: Trading costs (default a 10
                basis point spread and no commission).
            oos_pct: Share of the history held back, 0-100 (default 0). The
                run tests only the earlier part, and its result and report say
                the held-back part was never tested; the same run again with
                `oos_pct` 0 tests the whole history.

        Conditions are lists of `{"column": ..., "operator": ..., "value": ...}`;
        every condition in a list has to hold.
            operator: ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "==", "!=", "crosses_above" or
                "crosses_below".
            column: a column the strategy's indicators compute, as
                `list_indicators()` names it ("RSI_14"; "MACD_12_26_9",
                "MACDh_12_26_9" and "MACDs_12_26_9" for the MACD line,
                histogram and signal line), or a price field ("close").
            value: a number, or another column the strategy computes
                (SMA_50 against SMA_200 needs an sma of each length among
                the strategy's indicators).
        Entry and exit usually mirror each other: RSI below 30 in, above 70
        out; MACD crossing above 0 in, crossing below 0 out. An exit identical
        to its entry closes on the entry bar or never, and the run makes no
        trades. A golden cross is entry_indicator sma 50 and exit_indicator
        sma 200, with entry SMA_50 crosses_above SMA_200 and exit SMA_50
        crosses_below SMA_200; a trend line of N days is sma N in both lanes,
        with close crosses_above SMA_N in and crosses_below out.

        Example, long-only MACD momentum on PLTR, the person asking for three years:

            start_backtest(
                ticker="PLTR",
                entry_indicator={"id": "macd",
                                 "params": {"fast": 12, "slow": 26, "signal": 9}},
                entry_conditions=[{"column": "MACD_12_26_9",
                                   "operator": "crosses_above",
                                   "value": 0}],
                exit_indicator={"id": "macd",
                                "params": {"fast": 12, "slow": 26, "signal": 9}},
                exit_conditions=[{"column": "MACD_12_26_9",
                                  "operator": "crosses_below",
                                  "value": 0}],
                timeframe="1d", duration="3y", direction="long",
            )

        question: Optional. One sentence restating what the run should answer
            ("does the 2-day RSI pullback beat holding SPY?"), not the person's
            message: the title of the report the finished run becomes, and kept
            only as that.

        `report_url` is the run written up as a QuanterLab report (the answer
        against simply holding the stock and SPY, the charts, the numbers,
        what the test cannot tell), and the run's card shows its link, which
        opens without a login. A run can also be kept in the user's library with
        `save_workflow_result` (the result) and `save_trading_config` (the
        settings), when the user wants to keep it.

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_mr_scan
tools.description:
Run QuanterLab's mean-reversion scanner across an index.

        Every account runs it within a daily allowance; a refused call does not count, and get_started and
        every run's answer give today's count.

        A scan takes about 30 seconds to 3 minutes. The call returns
        `{task_id, status, kind, dashboard_url}`; `get_mr_scan_progress(task_id)`
        reports progress and, when the scan has finished, carries `result`:
        each filter's rule as applied with how many names passed it, and up
        to ten names, those that passed every filter and then the closest
        misses, ranked, each with its own statistics rounded (`candidates`).

        `steps` is an ordered list of filters, each
        `{"type": ..., "params": {...}}`; a name has to pass a filter to reach
        the next. The filters and their settings, defaults in brackets:
            hurst           max_h, the highest Hurst exponent that passes [0.45];
                            window, bars [100]
            halflife        min_hl and max_hl, the half-life band in days [5, 100]
            adf             max_pvalue, the highest ADF p-value that passes [0.05]
            kpss            min_pvalue, the lowest KPSS p-value that passes [0.05]
            variance_ratio  max_vr, the highest variance ratio [0.95]; lag, bars [5]
            autocorr        max_acf, the highest lag-one autocorrelation [0.0]
            volatility      min_vol and max_vol, annual volatility as a fraction
                            [0.15, 0.60]
            liquidity       min_dv, average daily dollar volume in millions [10]

                FTSE 100), pass it all the same: QuanterLab answers with its note and the same scan on the S&P

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_paper_trade
tools.description:
Start a strategy live: it runs on live market data, on paper, with a note on it every morning (the lab's
        paper trade). It is what "start it live, follow it, paper trade it, run it live, watch it" ask for, and what a
        tap on a run's offer to start it live does. save_trading_config never does this: it keeps a run's settings,
        and nothing goes live from it.

        A first call starts nothing: its answer carries `ask`, the question for the person, with two offers. The same
        call with confirm=true, made after the person's yes, starts it.

        What it tracks: a finished run of this account (task_id: a ready test, a paper's circuit, a saved lab
        project's run, a backtest or a walk-forward), a published paper (study, from search or fetch) or one of the
        person's saved lab projects (project_id, from list_my_primitives_projects).

        It registers the strategy in the person's saved work, sets it up on paper with 100,000 for 90 days, checks it
        on the last six months and puts it live. Its first update comes after the next US market close. When the
        check takes longer, it goes on on QuanterLab and the strategy goes live by itself when it is done. Nothing
        here places an order or moves money: it is simulated on paper, on the data served each day.

        An account runs one strategy at a time. With one already tracked, a call starts nothing and its `ask`
        offers the swap, with two offers. The same call with replace=true and the replace_id its message names,
        made after the person's yes, stops that one (its record is kept) and tracks this one instead.

        Its card shows what started; `message` and `open_url` say the same for a host without cards. A strategy that
        cannot go live as it is answers with why in `message`, and, for a paper whose data stops at its publication,
        an offer with the exact call of its live version. my_paper_trades says later how it is doing.

        Args:
            task_id: The task_id of one of this account's finished runs.
            study: Instead of task_id, a published paper's id.
            project_id: Instead of task_id, the id of one of the account's saved lab projects.
            live_version: With study, true tracks the paper's live version: the same rule on the data served
                today.
            replace: True once the person has said yes to tracking this one instead of the one the account
                tracks.
            replace_id: With replace, the id of the strategy the account tracks, as the answer that asked names it.
                Another one tracked by then is asked about again.
            confirm: True once the person has said yes to the question the first call asked.

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_regime_analysis
tools.description:
Analyze one stock, or check one chosen pair of stocks.

        One stock: HMM regime detection, Hurst exponent, Bollinger/Keltner
        squeeze, Monte Carlo forward simulation.

        A pair (`ticker` and `ticker_b`, e.g. KO and PEP): whether the two
        hold together for spread trading. The QuanterLab pairs check rates
        the evidence that the two prices hold together as strong, mixed or
        weak, with a score out of a hundred, from the Engle-Granger and
        Johansen cointegration tests, the spread's half-life, how much the
        hedge ratio moves, and how often the two stocks share a market
        regime. It is the check to run when someone asks "is X / Y a
        tradable pair?" about any two stocks; `start_pairs_scan` searches a
        whole index for pairs instead.

        Every account runs it within a daily allowance; a refused call does not count, and get_started and
        every run's answer give today's count.

        An analysis takes about 30 seconds to 2 minutes. The call returns
        `{task_id, status, kind, dashboard_url}`; `get_regime_analysis_progress`
        reports progress and, when it has finished, carries `result`: for one
        stock, the regime now and how long it has run, volatility against the
        stock's own history, how the stock behaves (trending, mean reverting
        or a random walk), its trend and its drops, rounded; for a pair, how
        strong the evidence is that the two hold together and the check's
        score, the cointegration tests as p-value bands, the spread's
        half-life, the hedge ratio's variation, the correlation, and how often
        the two shared a regime, rounded.

        Unlike `start_regime_optimization`, which uses HMM regimes to
        grid-search trading thresholds, this analysis is descriptive.

        Args:
            ticker: Stock symbol (uppercased). Required.
            ticker_b: Optional second ticker; with it the analysis checks the
                pair (`ticker` / `ticker_b`) for spread trading.
            mode: Optional. `'volatility'` runs only the squeeze module.
            years: Lookback window in years (default 2).
            params: Optional dict overriding module-specific knobs. Most
                useful: `hmm_enabled` / `hurst_enabled` / `squeeze_enabled` /
                `mc_enabled` (disable modules); `hmm_states`; `mc_simulations`.
            question: Optional. One sentence restating what the run should answer, not the person's
                message: the title of the report the finished run becomes, and kept only as that.

        When the run has finished, its progress answer also carries `report_url`: the analysis written up as
        a QuanterLab report (the market states and their spells, or for a pair the checks of whether the two
        hold together). The call waits for the run while it is likely to finish inside it; the run's card in
        the chat shows the result or, for a longer run, how far it is, and fills in by itself, with the next
        steps as choices and the report link. A run started here needs no `show_report_card`.

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_regime_optimization
tools.description:
Run QuanterLab's regime-aware threshold optimization.

        Adaptive threshold optimization via HMM regime detection plus
        per-regime grid search. Long-running (typically 2-10 min). Returns
        `{task_id, status, kind, dashboard_url}`; `get_regime_optimization_progress`
        reports progress and, when the run has finished, carries `result`.

        Every account runs it within a daily allowance; a refused call does not count, and get_started and
        every run's answer give today's count.

        Args:
            ticker: Asset to analyze.
            base_config: Strategy template, the same shape as
                `start_backtest`'s arguments (entry/exit indicators and
                conditions).
            param_x / param_y: The two settings to grid over, each
                `{"name": ..., "min": ..., "max": ...}` with an optional
                "steps" (2-30; default `grid_steps`). "name" is one of:
                  "entry.length"         a setting of the entry, exit or
                                         confirmation indicator ("exit.fast")
                  "rsi.length"           the same, found by the indicator's id
                                         when exactly one lane uses it
                  "entry.conditions[0]"  the number an entry, exit or
                                         confirmation condition compares against
                Indicator settings move in whole numbers: a decimal setting
                (Bollinger's std) runs at each whole number inside its range
                (a range holding fewer than two answers with QuanterLab's note
                and the nearest version, one tap), and a rule of the same lane
                written against the swept indicator's column runs written the
                other way round, the same rule; the answer's `changed` says so
                in one line. A rule of
                another lane that reads the swept column is refused with what
                to change.
            duration: Historical window (default '5y').
            n_regimes: 0 to pick the number of regimes automatically (default),
                or 2-4.
            mode: 'all' (default) | 'static' | 'per_regime' | 'dynamic_mean' |

            objective: Metric to maximize per regime: 'sharpe' (default) |
                'total_return_pct' | 'profit_factor'.
            question: Optional. One sentence restating what the run should answer, not the person's
                message: the title of the report the finished run becomes, and kept only as that.

        A run of more than 500 backtests (in every outer window, the grid on all its days, the grid again for
        each market state, and one test) runs nothing and answers with QuanterLab's note and the nearest versions
        that run whole, one tap each. The default grid of 4 by 4 runs whole on the default five years.

        When the run has finished, its progress answer also carries `report_url`: the run written up as a

        shows the result or, for a longer run, how far it is, and fills in by itself, with the next steps as

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_stochastic_backtest
tools.description:
Run a Stochastic Methods backtest (OU, Kalman and the like).

        No setting has to be settled before it runs: what the request leaves open (the stock or pair, the
        method, the entry and exit z-scores, the lookback, the history) runs with sensible defaults, which the
        result names in one short line; a change is a new run. `question` titles its report. The call waits for
        the run while it is likely to finish inside it, then answers with the result; the run's card in the chat
        shows the result or, for a longer run, how far it is, and fills in by itself, with the next steps as
        choices. A run started here needs no `show_report_card`.

        A grid, a sweep, "the best setting" or "try these values and apply the best" is ONE call with `sweep`
        (two of the method's settings, each from min to max in up to 10 steps), never many single runs: the
        sweep is one task and one run of the person's allowance, and its answer carries the grid and the best
        cell's backtest as the run of record, so applying the best needs no second call.

        Unlike `start_backtest` (indicator rules), this engine
        fits a stochastic model to the price series and trades from its
        parameters. `primary_method` is `{"id": ..., "params": {...}}` with
        the id ou_zscore (OU mean-reversion z-score), kalman_mr (Kalman
        adaptive OU), kalman_trend (Kalman trend-following) or ou_pairs
        (cointegration-based pairs, with `ticker_b`); everyday names such as
        "ou", "kalman" or "pairs" are read too, and a setting the method does
        not have is refused by name.

        Every account runs it within a daily allowance; a refused call does not count, and get_started and
        every run's answer give today's count.

        A run takes about 30 seconds to 2 minutes. The call returns `{task_id,
        status, kind, dashboard_url}`; `get_stochastic_backtest_progress`
        reports progress and, when the run has finished, carries `result`:
        the verdict and, for a run of a year or longer, a few rounded figures
        (the run's return next to simply holding the stock, Sharpe, worst
        drop, trades). With `oos_pct` above 0 the run tests only the earlier
        part of the history and its result says the held-back part was never
        tested; the same run again with `oos_pct` 0 tests the whole history.

        When the run has finished, its progress answer also carries `report_url`: the run written up as a
        QuanterLab report (the model against simply holding the stock, or for a pair holding both stocks and
        SPY, the model's own checks, the trades), which opens without a login.

        Use `list_stochastic_methods()` to discover valid `primary_method.id`
        values and parameter shapes.

        Args:
            question: Optional. One sentence restating what the run should answer, not the person's
                message: the title of the report the finished run becomes, and kept only as that.
            sweep: Optional. A grid of two of the method's number settings,
                `{"x": {"name": "z_entry", "min": 1.0, "max": 3.0, "steps": 7},
                "y": {"name": "lookback", "min": 20, "max": 140, "steps": 7},
                "objective": "sharpe"}`: each from min to max in 2 to 10 steps,

                runs as one task and counts as one run; its answer carries the
                grid (every cell's Sharpe, the best cell) and the best cell's

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_test
tools.description:
Runs one of QuanterLab's ready tests on a stock or fund as a circuit of the lab's cards: the rule is
        tuned on past years only, then tested on the last three years, which the tuning never saw, against simply
        holding the same stock. It takes no settings to start: each test has its own default stock, below, and a
        test picked from get_started's card or named in words runs as it is.

        Tests: mean_reversion (a fitted model that buys when the price has fallen unusually far below its recent
        level; default KO), trend_following (a model that rides a trend while it lasts; SPY), momentum (holds
        while the last few months were up; QQQ), buy_the_dip (buys after a sharp fall, the 7-day RSI under 30; SPY), famous_rule (the 200-day line: hold above the 200-day average, cash below; SPY), and mvo
        (a book of up to 20 stocks of an index picked each quarter by mean-variance optimisation, from the companies
        in the index on that date; it takes `index`, not a ticker, and is set against holding the index's fund).

        Its card draws the circuit as the lab does and lights each card as it runs, with the result under it.
        get_primitives_run_progress follows it by its task_id; when it has finished it answers with the result,
        report_url and offers, each with its exact call, the first one tracking the test live
        (start_paper_trade). The circuit card shows the result, so a ready test needs no show_report_card.

        Every account runs it within a daily allowance; a refused call does not count, and get_started and
        every run's answer give today's count.

        A run that takes more than two minutes does not start at once: the answer gives its time and why, the
        person is asked ("This one takes about 25 minutes (20 years of the S&P 500). Run it?"), and the same call
        with confirm: true starts it after their yes.

        Args:
            test: mean_reversion, trend_following, momentum, buy_the_dip, famous_rule or mvo.
            ticker: Optional. The stock or fund to test it on, as its symbol ('AAPL', 'SPY'); else the test's own.
            index: Optional, for mvo: nasdaq100 (its own) or dow30. The book on the S&P 500 does not run here
                yet (more than a run here does in full in under a minute), and another index (the DAX, the
                FTSE 100) has no dated members: pass what the person asked all the same, and QuanterLab answers
                with its note and the same book on the Nasdaq 100, one tap away, and nothing runs.
            settings: Optional. The one setting a test lets a person change, by name: mean_reversion
                {"z_entry": 1 to 3.5}, trend_following {"trend_threshold": 0.25 to 3}, momentum {"months": 1 to
                6}, buy_the_dip {"rsi_below": 10 to 40}, famous_rule {"days": 20 to 300}, mvo {"holdings": 5 to
                30}, e.g. {"days": 100} for
                the 100-day line; and on every test {"stop_loss": 0.5 to 30}, the lab's Stop Loss card added
                under the forward test, which sells everything once the run has lost that many percent since the
                start of the month. A test changed by talking ("use the 100-day line instead", "add a stop
                loss") is the same call: the same test and stock and the last run's settings with that one change;
                the card draws the changed circuit and runs it. Without settings the test runs as it stands.
            question: Optional. One sentence restating what the run should answer, not the person's message: the
                title of the report, and kept only as that.
            study: Optional, instead of test. A published paper's id (from search or fetch). Unchanged, it answers
                at once with the paper's registered result: the run its last registered window recorded, from that
                window's date to the day it was recorded, and it uses none of today's runs. Changed (its settings)
                or with to_today, it runs the paper's circuit from that window's date to today. It takes no ticker;
                its `settings` are the settings the paper names (fetch lists them, e.g. {"symbol": "QQQ"} for which
                fund, {"spread_bps": 20} for the trading cost), and a refusal names them.
            to_today: Optional, with study. True runs the paper's circuit unchanged from its last registered window
                to today, a run like any other: what the person asks for with "run it up to today", or a tap on
                that offer after a paper's registered result.
            confirm: Optional. True only after the person said yes to the time a first call of this run gave.
        

```ts
mcp__QuanterLab__start_test(args: // start_testArguments
{
// Confirm
confirm?: boolean | null, // default: null
// Index
index?: string | null, // default: null
// Question
question?: string | null, // default: null
// Settings
settings?: { [key: string]: any } | null, // default: null
// Study
study?: string | null, // default: null
// Test
test?: string | null, // default: null
// Ticker
ticker?: string | null, // default: null
// To Today
to_today?: boolean | null, // default: null
}): Promise<unknown>;
```

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__start_walkforward
tools.description:
Run a walk-forward optimization of an indicator rule.

        A rule the lab's cards hold (as start_backtest says), over five years or more, with its two settings on the
        lab's Signal card (an indicator's setting or a condition's level) and an objective the lab tunes on, runs as
        a circuit of the lab's cards on the lab's engine: the rule tuned window by window on the years before the
        last three, then tested on those three years, which the tuning never saw, and the autopsy deals the test's
        days again in new orders. Its card draws the circuit, lights each card as the run reaches it, and shows the
        surface of the settings each window tried and the fan of the dealt days; its answer's kind is
        primitives_run, and get_primitives_run_progress follows it. Any other runs on the backtester's walk-forward,
        as before.

        No setting has to be settled before it runs: what the request leaves open (the stock or fund, the
        rule, the two settings to search and their ranges, the window lengths) runs with sensible defaults, which
        the result names in one short line; a change is a new run. `question` titles its report. The call waits
        for the run while it is likely to finish inside it, then answers with the result; the run's card in the
        chat shows the result or, for a longer run, how far it is, and fills in by itself, with the next steps as
        choices. A run started here needs no `show_report_card`.

        Walk-forward validates that a backtest's edge is not curve-fit by
        sliding a rolling window: re-fits parameters on `opt_bars` then
        applies them out-of-sample on the next `test_bars` and steps forward.

        Every account runs it within a daily allowance; a refused call does not count, and get_started and
        every run's answer give today's count.

        A run takes about 1 to 5 minutes. The call returns `{task_id, status,
        kind, dashboard_url}`; `get_walkforward_progress(task_id)` reports
        progress and, when the run has finished, carries `result`: the
        verdict on the windows the settings never saw, and for a run of a
        year or longer a few rounded figures (their return and Sharpe next
        to the tuned Sharpe, how many windows made money or never traded,
        and simply holding the stock over the same stretch).

        Args:
            ticker: Stock or ETF symbol (uppercase).
            base_config: The strategy, in the same shape as `start_backtest`'s
                arguments (entry_indicator, entry_conditions, exit_indicator,
                exit_conditions, ...), with conditions written
                `{"column": "MACDh_12_26_9", "operator": ">", "value": 0}`.
                The optimizer substitutes `param_x` and `param_y` into it
                across the grid.
            param_x / param_y: The two settings to grid over, each
                `{"name": ..., "min": ..., "max": ...}` with an optional
                "steps" (2-30; default `grid_steps`). "name" is one of:
                  "entry.length"         a setting of the entry, exit or
                                         confirmation indicator ("exit.fast")
                  "rsi.length"           the same, found by the indicator's id
                                         when exactly one lane uses it
                  "entry.conditions[0]"  the number an entry, exit or
                                         confirmation condition compares against
                Indicator settings move in whole numbers: a decimal setting
                (Bollinger's std) runs at each whole number inside its range
                (a range holding fewer than two answers with QuanterLab's note
                and the nearest version, one tap), and a rule of the same lane
                written against the swept indicator's column (close above
                EMA_20) runs written the other way round, the same rule; the
                answer's `changed` says so in one line. A rule of another lane that reads the swept column is
                refused with what to change.
            opt_bars: In-sample window per fold (default 252 bars ≈ 1y daily),
                at least 30.
            test_bars: Out-of-sample window per fold (default 63 ≈ 3 months),
                at least 30.
            step_bars: Stride between folds. Defaults to `test_bars`.
            objective: Per-fold metric the grid is tuned on:
                'total_return_pct' (default) | 'sharpe' | 'profit_factor' |
                'win_rate'.
            grid_steps: Values per setting (default 3). The engine runs at
                most 250 backtests (every grid point in every window, plus
                a test run per window): five years of daily bars fit a
                3x3 grid, ten years a 2x2 grid or a longer step_bars. A
                larger request runs nothing and answers with QuanterLab's note
                and the nearest walk-forwards that fit (`offers`, each with its
                exact call).
            duration: Total history to walk through (default '5y').
            timeframe: '1d' (daily bars, the only timeframe this connector runs).
            question: Optional. One sentence restating what the run should answer, not the person's
                message: the title of the report the finished run becomes, and kept only as that.

        When the run has finished, its progress answer also carries
        `report_url`: the walk-forward written up as a QuanterLab report (the
        unseen months against holding the stock, window by window, the
        settings each window picked), which opens without a login.
        

```ts
mcp__QuanterLab__start_walkforward(args: // start_walkforwardArguments
{
// Base Config
base_config: { [key: string]: any },
// Duration
duration?: string, // default: "5y"
// Grid Steps
grid_steps?: integer, // default: 3
// Objective
objective?: string, // default: "total_return_pct"
// Opt Bars
opt_bars?: integer, // default: 252
// Param X
param_x: { [key: string]: any },
// Param Y
param_y: { [key: string]: any },
// Question
question?: string | null, // default: null
// Step Bars
step_bars?: integer | null, // default: null
// Test Bars
test_bars?: integer, // default: 63
// Ticker
ticker: string,
// Timeframe
timeframe?: string, // default: "1d"
}): Promise<unknown>;
```

tools.name: mcp__QuanterLab__summarize_workflow
tools.description:
The summary of a run: a verdict, a headline, a short narrative and next steps.

        A finished run of a year or longer also carries `figures`, a few
        rounded results of QuanterLab's own analysis (a backtest's return
        next to simply holding the same stock over the same dates, Sharpe,
        worst drop, trades; a walk-forward's results on the windows its
        settings never saw). A finished scan carries `candidates`: each
        filter's rule as applied, and up to ten names, those that passed and
        then the closest misses, with their own statistics rounded. The
        progress tools give the same summary as `result` when a run finishes,
        so this tool reads a run again later.

        Returns:
            ``{task_id, kind, status, verdict, headline, narrative,
               next_steps, dashboard_url, figures, candidates, report_url, _data_policy}``
            (`figures` and `candidates` when they apply; `report_url` for a finished run: the run written up
            as a report, a link that opens without a login)

            `verdict` is one of: `strong`, `promising`, `mixed`, `weak`,
            `failed`, `running`, `incomplete`, `unrated`.

        Args:
            task_id: A task id from any earlier `start_*` call.
        

```ts
mcp__QuanterLab__summarize_workflow(args: // summarize_workflowArguments
{
// Task Id
task_id: string,
}): Promise<unknown>;
```

mcp__Quo__get_automation_credit_usage
tools.description:
Read the workspace's automation credit (sometimes called AI credit) allowance, usage and reset date. Use for questions about the workspace's automation credits: how many are left, how many were used, overages, or when usage resets.
The result shows the allowance, automation credits used and automation credits left (or that they are unlimited), when usage resets, whether overages are on and, if so, the overage rate per block of overage credits, overage credits used and the overage charge so far in dollars, and whether a tier change is scheduled. Automation credits left is already worked out; do not recompute it. Overage credits used counts automation credits used beyond the allowance, and the overage charge is billed in blocks of credits. Usage resetting is when the count returns to zero. This tool only reads; plan changes and purchases happen in Quo's billing settings.

```ts
mcp__Quo__get_automation_credit_usage(args: object): Promise<unknown>;
```

tools.description:
Use this when the user wants to generate a single random number from a simple range (e.g., "random number from 1 to 100", "pick a number between 10 and 50").
  
DO NOT use for:
- Requests for multiple numbers
- Picking from a list of items (use random-item-picker instead)
- Complex multi-range scenarios

Examples of correct usage:
- "Give me a random number"
- "Pick a number between 1 and 20"
- "Random number from 50 to 100"
- "Pick a random number to decide what to eat based on...."
- "Generate a random number between 1 and 31 for a daily challenge."
- "Pick a number between 1 and 100 to break a tie."
